title: Gen Z groups and Mayor Sampang meet the army chief at Army Headquarters

Crowds outside chanted different names (Karki, Balen Shah, Harka Sampang) and soldiers told them to agree among themselves and return the next day.

title: Ten left parties merge into the Nepali Communist Party

title: Gen Z activists and police clash at Simara Chowk, Bara

Police arrested three people, including two ward chairs elected from UML; three others remained at large. Gen Z leaders accused police of security lapses. evidence.note: Date inferred: the article of Friday 21 November 2025 refers to 'Wednesday's clash'.

The Kathmandu Post gives disagreement over distribution of portfolios as the sole reason.

title: House of Representatives election

properties.summary: Election to the 275-member House of Representatives, the first since the September 2025 uprising, held on the date set on 12 September 2025. Turnout was about 60 per cent. The RSP won 125 of 165 direct seats and 57 proportional seats, 182 in total; Nepali Congress 38; CPN-UML 25. Balendra Shah beat Oli in Jhapa-5 by 49,614 votes. Interim counts and analyst estimates ran ahead of the final total (an estimate of 185-190 seats on 9 March; 119 direct seats at an interim count).

evidence.note: Final totals from RTHK and Wikipedia; interim and forecast numbers differ and are described in the summary.

title: Karki commission submits report on 8-9 September events

properties.summary: The three-member commission chaired by Gauri Bahadur Karki handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on Sunday 8 March 2026, after questioning about 200 people. Outlets give different lengths (1,000 pages; 8,000-10,000 pages). The report recommended criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung under Sections 181 and 182, and departmental action against police, Armed Police and Army officers. After outlets published its content, Karki decided on about 25 March to release it formally.

evidence.note: Report length is disputed; see the two report-length claims.

title: Balendra Shah sworn in as prime minister

title: Former PM Oli and former Home Minister Lekhak arrested

title: Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods

title: First anniversary: Gen Z Martyrs' Day

properties.summary: Nepal observed 8 September 2026 as Gen Z Martyrs' Day, a public holiday. A programme by the GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society in New Baneshwor was attended by the Home Minister, ministers and families. Hamro Patro says 76 people died and the government has declared 45 martyrs; embassies including Australia, Norway, the UK, the US and Japan posted messages. An injured protester told Africanews the injured still needed state support.

evidence.note: Death toll given as 76 by Hamro Patro and 77 by IANS.

title: Parties issue contrasting statements on the anniversary

IANS summarises that the RSP played down property destruction while opposition parties stressed it.

title: UML vice-chair and general secretary submit opposing reports on Oli

title: Nepali Congress 15th general convention

properties.summary: Leaders of the Congress, RSP, Nepali Communist Party and UML spoke at the Congress general convention at Khula Manch (Tundikhel), pledging cooperation on democracy and the constitution. Gagan Thapa criticised the prime minister's absence from Parliament; Dahal and UML's Pokharel raised fears of authoritarianism. Thapa's interview of the same date places the start on 6 October and refers to a parallel convention by Sher Bahadur Deuba.

evidence.note: The Kathmandu Post's convention report is dated 5 October and quotes speeches, while its interview of 5 October says the convention begins on 6 October.

title: Temple-gate festival clip shared as an attack on Pashupatinath Temple

properties.caption: Clip of a crowd gripping and climbing the gates of Pashupatinath Temple, shared on 9 September 2025 as protesters attacking the temple. Fact-checkers traced it to a festival procession in March 2025.

page_url.label: X post of 9 September 2025 presenting a temple-gate clip as an attack on Pashupatinath Temple

properties.location_method: Chronolocation and place by BOOM, Alt News and Newschecker. BOOM and Newschecker traced keyframes by reverse-image search to a Facebook reel dated 14 July 2025 (https://www.facebook.com/reel/10043049515803499) and to a TikTok post of 31 March 2025 (https://www.tiktok.com/@/video/7487826733312249118). BOOM says the TikTok uploader confirmed he filmed it around the end of March 2025. Newschecker says the admin of the Facebook festival page confirmed it was recorded on 31 March 2025. Alt News matched attire between keyframes and the 14 July TikTok and noted a similar 2023 clip. The festival is not agreed: BOOM names the Basleshwori (Basleshwari) Jatra, Alt News and Newschecker the Naxal Bhagwati Jatra (see claim:pashupatinath-video-festival-and-date-conflict). Alt News adds that knocking on the temple gate is a ceremonial part of that festival. The viral X post is recorded by URL only; NDTV India also aired the clip, per BOOM, and its Instagram post has since been deleted. Coordinates basis: Wikipedia coordinates as recorded in location:pashupatinath-temple. URL check: X oEmbed 200 on 2026-10-05.
properties.verified_by: BOOM; Alt News; Newschecker

evidence.note: URL, platform and date as cited by the fact-checkers; checked by oEmbed where the platform offers it (see location_method).
What the clip really shows and when, as the fact-checkers established it.
Flagged misattributed or recycled by the named fact-checkers; method as they describe it.

title: Onlinekhabar drone video: protesters reach the Parliament building (8 September 2025)

properties.caption: Drone video posted by Onlinekhabar on 8 September 2025, captioned that Gen Z reached the Parliament building by breaking the police cordon.
